title: Fixed vocabulary
note: The only words and colours the dashboard is allowed to use for direction, tone, cycle stage and where a fact came from. Every colour here was checked with a colour-blindness and contrast validator against a white background. Every item carries a plainLabel so no visitor has to know finance words.

trajectoryFlags.label: Accelerating
trajectoryFlags.meaning: Growing, and growing faster than last quarter.

trajectoryFlags.label: Steady
trajectoryFlags.meaning: Moving along at about the same pace.

trajectoryFlags.label: Decelerating
trajectoryFlags.meaning: Still growing, but slower than last quarter.

trajectoryFlags.label: Inflecting Up
trajectoryFlags.meaning: Was falling, has just started to rise.

trajectoryFlags.label: Inflecting Down
trajectoryFlags.meaning: Was rising, has just started to fall.

steps.label: Confident
steps.meaning: Sure of themselves. Talks about growth and new spending.

steps.label: Neutral
steps.meaning: Neither good nor bad. Wait and see.

steps.label: Cautious
steps.meaning: Holding back. Talks about risks and delays.

steps.label: Defensive
steps.meaning: Protecting the business. Talks about cutting costs.

cycleStages.label: Trough
cycleStages.meaning: Spending is at its lowest. Nothing is being ordered.

cycleStages.label: Early Upcycle
cycleStages.meaning: First new orders are landing. Only the early movers feel it.

cycleStages.label: Mid Upcycle
cycleStages.meaning: Orders are broad. Most of the sector is busy.

cycleStages.label: Late Upcycle/Peak
cycleStages.meaning: Everyone is at full stretch. Costs are climbing.

cycleStages.label: Early Downcycle
cycleStages.meaning: New orders are thinning out. The early movers slow first.

sourceTags.label: Official
sourceTags.meaning: Published by a government body or regulator.

sourceTags.label: Company Filing
sourceTags.meaning: Taken straight from a company's own filed results.

sourceTags.label: Mgmt Claim
sourceTags.meaning: Something management stated but nobody has checked.

sourceTags.label: External
sourceTags.meaning: From a news report, broker note or industry body.

sourceTags.label: Estimate
sourceTags.meaning: A forward guess, not a reported number.

sourceTags.label: Inference
sourceTags.meaning: A conclusion drawn from what was said, not stated outright.

sourceTags.label: Derived
sourceTags.meaning: Calculated by this dashboard from other data on this page.

sourceTags.label: Unknown
sourceTags.meaning: We do not know where this came from. Treat with care.

standingSix.plainDescription: Six slots that get read every quarter no matter what, because between them they cover the whole chain from drilling to fuel pumps.

slots.label: ONGC
slots.why: The biggest spender. If it stops ordering, the cycle stops.

slots.label: Deep Industries / Jindal Drilling
slots.why: The rigs get hired first. The earliest hard signal there is.

slots.label: Reliance
slots.why: Sets the tone for refining and petrochemicals.

slots.label: Engineers India
slots.why: Its order book is a preview of the next few years of projects.

slots.label: Petronet LNG
slots.why: Shows how much imported gas the country is actually using.

slots.label: IOCL / BPCL
slots.why: Fuel demand at the pump, plus the biggest refinery spending plans.

stageActions.plainDescription: The research shortlist, mapped to the cycle stage. When the stage call changes this list changes with it, and every row says which stage it came from.
stageActions.note: AUTHORED IN-REPO, NOT EXTRACTED. These rows are editorial guidance, not data about any company: no number here is claimed to come from a filing. Replace the text with the client's own stage-5b wording and the panel picks it up with no code change.

trough.action: Check enquiry and tendering volumes at the drillers and EPC names
trough.why: Enquiries move before order inflow does, so they are the first hard evidence a bottom is real.

trough.action: Screen the leveraged names for covenant and refinancing risk
trough.why: A trough is where balance sheets decide who is still there for the recovery.

trough.action: Read ONGC and Oil India capex guidance for the coming year
trough.why: Upstream capex is the budget every service order is eventually paid from.

early-upcycle.action: Track order inflow and book-to-bill at the early movers
early-upcycle.why: This is the stage where inflow turns before revenue does; the gap is the opportunity.

early-upcycle.action: Check rig and asset utilisation, and day-rate direction
early-upcycle.why: Utilisation tightening ahead of pricing is the classic early-upcycle tell.

early-upcycle.action: Confirm the refiners and shippers have NOT yet turned
early-upcycle.why: If the back of the chain has already moved, the call is later than early upcycle.

early-upcycle.action: Ask who is adding capacity, and at what cost
early-upcycle.why: Capacity added early earns the whole cycle; added late it defines the next downturn.

mid-upcycle.action: Watch margins, not just volumes, across the coincident names
mid-upcycle.why: Mid-cycle is where pricing power shows up or fails to.

mid-upcycle.action: Check execution and order-book conversion against guidance
mid-upcycle.why: A book that stops converting is the first crack in a broad upcycle.

mid-upcycle.action: Track input costs and pass-through at the pipe and equipment makers
mid-upcycle.why: Steel and freight decide whether a strong order book earns anything.

late-upcycle.action: Read the leading group for the first signs of rolling over
late-upcycle.why: The front of the chain turns down first, and it is the only free warning available.

late-upcycle.action: Count the capacity being commissioned across the sector
late-upcycle.why: Supply added at the peak is what makes the next downcycle long.

late-upcycle.action: Check how far forward contracts and day-rates are locked
late-upcycle.why: Contract cover is what separates a soft landing from a sharp one.

early-downcycle.action: Move to cash generation and net debt at every name held
early-downcycle.why: In a downcycle the question stops being growth and becomes survival and optionality.

early-downcycle.action: Check the regulated and volume-linked names for relative shelter
early-downcycle.why: City gas and transmission volumes decay far more slowly than capex does.

early-downcycle.action: Watch for order deferrals, cancellations and slipping delivery dates
early-downcycle.why: Cancellations show up in commentary a quarter before they show up in the numbers.
